transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for having me. I, um... I hope I'm doing this right. 

It's a little embarrassing to talk about, honestly, and I really don't want you to think I'm just some difficult, complaining neighbor. I try very hard to be easy to get along with. But... well, for nearly two years now, I’ve just been sure that our contractor and some of the people on our block have been quietly working together to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband, he's very patient, and he keeps showing me the receipts, and the workers always have so many excuses... but I just know what they're doing. 

I hope it's okay that I start with that... am I explaining it alright?
You feel strongly that the contractor and your neighbors are working against you, is that right?

Yes... yes, Doctor, that's exactly it. I know it must sound just awful when you say it back to me like that. I really do hate to accuse anyone, I promise I'm not usually a suspicious or mean-spirited person. 

But... well, like I was saying, it's been almost two whole years of this. They just keep that kitchen unfinished and wrong on purpose. And... and no matter how many times my husband pulls out the paper trails and the receipts to try and calm me down, or how many polite little excuses the workers give us... I just know they're all in on it together. 

Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound too dreadful saying all this out loud to you.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, confirming your suspicions about the contractor and neighbors?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I... I hope I haven't made you think I'm, well, losing my mind or anything. I promise I don't hear any voices or sounds that aren't really there. 

I would absolutely tell you if I did, because I want to be as helpful as I can and do this properly. But no, it's really just... just what I see with my own two eyes, and the way they act when I ask about the cabinets. I don't hear anything unusual. 

Did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Is your concern about the contractor and neighbors cheating you limited to the kitchen renovation, or do you think they might be plotting against you in other areas of your life as well?

Oh, well, um... no, it's really just the kitchen. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I know how that sounds. It's just... the kitchen is such a big project, and it's taking so long, and it just feels like they're dragging their feet on purpose. 

But no, I don't think they're trying to ruin my whole life or anything. I'm sure they're perfectly nice people in other ways. It's just this one thing with the cabinets and the flooring. I try to be reasonable about it, I really do. 

Is that what you meant? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you ever feel like people are plotting against you or cheating you in situations outside of the kitchen renovation?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I might not have explained myself very well just a second ago. But no, absolutely not. It really is just confined to the kitchen situation. 

I promise I don't go around thinking the cashier at the grocery store or the ladies at my church are out to get me! I'm actually a very trusting person normally, I really am. I'd hate for you to think I'm just... well, sitting around being suspicious of everyone in my life. It's truly just this one terrible mess with the house. 

Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking, Doctor.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misinterpreting the situation with the contractor and your neighbors?

Oh, well... I mean, I suppose anyone can make a mistake, right? I try to be very open-minded, I really do. But... well, I've been dealing with this for nearly two years now. Two whole years. 

I know my husband tries to make me feel better—he shows me the receipts and the contracts, and the contractor always has some perfectly polite excuse. And I smile and nod because I don't want to cause a fuss. But... I just know they're quietly working together, the contractor and a few of the people on my block. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, just to cheat us. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so stubborn of me. I really don't want to be difficult, and I know you must hear all sorts of things. But I just can't shake what I see happening right in front of me. Am I being too difficult? I really am trying to look at it from all sides, Doctor.
Do you think your beliefs about the contractor and neighbors might be exaggerated or not entirely based in reality?

Oh, goodness... well, I really do try to ask myself that. I don't want to be one of those people who just makes up stories, you know? I want to be reasonable. I really, really do. 

But... well, it's just that I've been dealing with this for almost two years now. And I know my husband tries so hard to reassure me. He brings out all the paperwork, the receipts, everything, and the contractor always has these very polite, perfectly reasonable-sounding excuses. And I listen, I really do! I don't want to be a bother to anyone. 

But deep down... I just know they're quietly working together. The contractor and those few neighbors on my block. They're just stringing us along, keeping the kitchen half-wrong on purpose to cheat us. I know how it sounds, and I'm so sorry if it seems like I'm not listening to reason. I just... I can't ignore what I know is happening, no matter how many excuses they give. 

I hope you don't think I'm completely out of touch with reality, Doctor. I really am trying my best to handle this gracefully. Am I making sense?
How certain are you that the contractor and neighbors are working together to cheat you?

Oh, dear... I know I probably sound like a broken record, and I'm so sorry to keep saying the same things over and over. But... well, to answer your question, I am completely certain. 

I really wish I wasn't! I would love nothing more than to just be making a silly mistake about all this. But for nearly two years now, I've just been absolutely sure that the contractor and those people on my block are quietly working together to cheat us. They are keeping that kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and I just know it in my bones—no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many polite excuses they come up with. 

I wouldn't insist on it if I wasn't entirely sure, Doctor. I really hope I don't sound too stubborn or difficult saying that... I'm just trying to be as honest with you as I can. Is it alright that I'm being this blunt about it?
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you could be mistaken about the contractor and neighbors working together to cheat you?

Oh, my... I know I must be frustrating you so much by not just saying yes. I really, really want to be agreeable, Doctor. I'd love to just say there's a chance I'm wrong, just to make things easier for everyone. I hate being a bother. 

But... well, like I've been saying, it's been two whole years of this. I've tried, I really have. I've looked at all those receipts my husband shows me, and I've listened to every single excuse they give, but... I just can't deny what's happening. I know they're working together to cheat us and keep that kitchen half-wrong on purpose. 

I'm so sorry, I feel dreadful being so unbending about it when you're just trying to help me see it differently. I hope you aren't too upset with me for sticking to this... I just can't say I'm mistaken when I know what they're doing. Is it okay that I'm being so firm about this? I really don't want to be a difficult patient for you.
Do you think your belief about the contractor and neighbors cheating you could be a delusion?

Oh, goodness... a delusion? That's such a strong word, isn't it? It makes me sound like I'm... well, crazy. And I really, really hope you don't think I'm crazy, Doctor. I'm just a normal person, I promise you. 

I know it must sound so strange to you, and I feel just awful keeping on about it. But... well, I'm only here talking to you because for nearly two years now, I've just been so sure about this. The contractor and those few people on my block... they really are quietly working together to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. 

I know my husband shows me the receipts, and I know they always have an excuse for why things aren't finished right, and I try so hard to just accept it so I don't cause a fuss. But I just know what's happening. 

I'm so sorry if that's not the answer you were hoping for. I really don't want to be difficult or seem like I'm not listening to you. I just... I don't think it's a delusion when it's really happening, you know? Does that make sense? I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying that.
Do you think you could ever consider the possibility that your interpretation of the situation with the contractor and neighbors might not be accurate?

Oh, dear... I know I'm probably testing your patience right now, and I'm so, so sorry. I really want to be the kind of patient who just nods and takes your advice, because I know you're the expert and you're just trying to help me. I hate feeling like I'm being stubborn with you. 

But... oh, it's just so hard to even imagine it not being true. I know I've said it a dozen times today, and I'm sorry to repeat myself, but for almost two years I've just been so certain. The contractor and those folks on my street, they really are working together to cheat us. They're keeping the kitchen half-wrong on purpose. 

I try to look at it differently, I really do. My husband shows me the receipts, and they give me all these polite little excuses, and I try to tell myself, 'Maybe I'm just getting confused in my old age.' But then I see what they're doing, and I just know. 

I'm so sorry, Doctor. I'd love to tell you that I could see it another way, just to make you happy. I hope you aren't too frustrated with me... I'm doing my best to be a good patient, I promise. Is it terribly awful of me that I just can't see it any other way?
Have you had any other thoughts or beliefs that you're completely certain about, but others might find hard to understand or disagree with?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing else at all. I know I've been going on and on about the kitchen and the contractor, and I'm so sorry if it makes me seem like I'm just... well, full of strange ideas. But I promise you, it's really just this one specific situation. 

Everything else in my life is perfectly normal, I assure you. I keep a nice tidy house, I get along with my family, and I don't have any other... um, unusual thoughts or big disagreements with anyone. I really try my very best to be agreeable and easy to get along with in every other part of my life. 

I hope that's a good sign? I'd just hate for you to think I'm a difficult or argumentative person all around. I'm really not, Doctor, I promise. Did I answer that okay for you?
